title.purpose: Pane headings and modal/section titles only (20px, 19px, 15px variants share this role).

body.purpose: The base UI size — nearly all text in the app.

small.purpose: Secondary text — hints, sub-labels, result rows, muted supporting lines under a heading.

micro.purpose: Compact badges and tags (.tag, event badges) where Label's uppercase 12px treatment would be too loud.

label.purpose: Uppercase structural labels: table headers, form group labels, section headers.

shadows.name: shadow-1
shadows.purpose: The lightest lift in the elevation scale (redesign v2 foundation, new token) — currently wired only to a segmented control's pressed option (`.seg button[aria-pressed="true"]`); otherwise reserved for future fine-grained use.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: `--shadow` / `--shadow-2`: the general floating-chrome shadow, paired with Glass fill on menus/popovers (dialogs, toasts, and the save bar instead pair Float's heavier sibling, Shadow-3).

shadows.name: shadow-3
shadows.purpose: The heavier lift for Glass-Heavy surfaces — popovers/menus, dialogs, toasts, the save bar, the auth card, the evp-dialog, and the Playback/Events touch drawers — usually paired with an inset Glass Highlight top edge (`inset 0 1px 0 var(--glass-highlight)`).

shadows.name: shadow-float
shadows.purpose: `--shadow-float` (documented in DESIGN.md as Hover-Lift): a live-grid tile (`.tile:hover`) or an Events card (`.ev-card:hover`) under a real pointer, gated on `(hover: hover)`, paired with `translateY(-2px)` to `-3px`.

motion.name: dur-instant
motion.purpose: Renumbered in the foundation pass (new token, was not a separate step before). Reserved for the snappiest micro-feedback; not yet wired to a specific rule as of this pass.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Renumbered from .15s. Hover/press micro-feedback: button background/border/filter transitions, `.btn:active{scale(.96)}`, segmented-control and nav-link state changes, the toggle-switch knob.

motion.name: dur-base
motion.purpose: Renumbered from .2s. Zoom/pan transforms and general mid-weight UI motion.

motion.name: dur-slow
motion.purpose: Renumbered from .22s. Larger UI motion: slide-ins, auto-hiding playback controls.

motion.name: dur-chrome-out
motion.purpose: New token (foundation pass): the duration for glass chrome (touch drawers, fullscreen side panels) animating closed/away.

motion.name: dur-chrome-in
motion.purpose: New token (foundation pass): the duration for glass chrome animating into view — intentionally slower than chrome-out so entrances read as settling, not snapping.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Default easing for ordinary UI motion: `.btn`, `.seg button`, nav/tile hover and press transitions.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Material-style standard easing, defined alongside the others; general-purpose fallback.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Symmetric ease for motion with no clear directional bias.

motion.name: ease-spring
motion.purpose: Overshoot spring, defined for gesture-release and toggle-confirmation moments.

motion.name: spring-gentle
motion.purpose: New token (foundation pass): a softer, lower-overshoot spring than `--ease-spring`, used for glass chrome settling into place.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one emphasized action in a group — save, confirm, primary CTA. Fully pill-shaped (redesign v2 foundation, was an 8px-radius rectangle) with real press feedback.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 7px; height: 36px; padding: 0 16px; border-radius: var(--r-full, 999px); border: 1px solid var(--line-2, #2c2c31); background: var(--panel-2, #222226); font: 600 14px/1 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: transform var(--dur-fast, .18s) var(--ease-out-expo, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)), background var(--dur-fast, .18s) var(--ease-out-expo, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)), border-color var(--dur-fast, .18s) var(--ease-out-expo, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)), filter var(--dur-fast, .18s) var(--ease-out-expo, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)); } .ds-btn:active { transform: scale(.96); } .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--accent, #0074e8); border-color: var(--accent, #0074e8); color: var(--accent-ink, #ffffff); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.08); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #0074e8); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Default button style for non-primary actions (the plain `.btn`) — pill-shaped, bordered, no fill emphasis.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 7px; height: 36px; padding: 0 16px; border-radius: var(--r-full, 999px); font: 600 14px/1 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color var(--dur-fast, .18s) var(--ease-out-expo, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)); } .ds-btn:active { transform: scale(.96); } .ds-btn-secondary { background: var(--panel-2, #222226); border: 1px solid var(--line-2, #2c2c31); color: var(--text, #f5f5f7); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: var(--faint, #6e6e73); }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Low-emphasis action, transparent until hovered — same pill shape and 600-weight label as every other button.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 7px; height: 36px; padding: 0 16px; border-radius: var(--r-full, 999px); border: 1px solid transparent; font: 600 14px/1 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background var(--dur-fast, .18s) var(--ease-out-expo, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)), color var(--dur-fast, .18s) var(--ease-out-expo, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)); } .ds-btn:active { transform: scale(.96); } .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: var(--muted, #a1a1a6); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--panel-2, #222226); color: var(--text, #f5f5f7); }

components.name: Segmented Control
components.description: The `.seg` view/filter switcher — fully pill-shaped and borderless now (redesign v2 foundation, was a bordered 9px-radius rectangle); its pressed option lifts on a Panel background with the Shadow-1 token.
components.css: .ds-seg { display: inline-flex; padding: 3px; border-radius: var(--r-full, 999px); background: var(--panel-2, #222226); border: 0; } .ds-seg button { border: 0; background: transparent; height: 28px; padding: 0 14px; border-radius: var(--r-full, 999px); color: var(--muted, #a1a1a6); font-weight: 600; font-size: 14px; cursor: pointer; transition: background var(--dur-fast, .18s) var(--ease-out-expo, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)), color var(--dur-fast, .18s) var(--ease-out-expo, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)); } .ds-seg button[aria-pressed="true"] { background: var(--panel, #18181b); color: var(--text, #f5f5f7); box-shadow: var(--shadow-1, 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.4)); }

components.name: Live-Count Pill
components.description: The `.pill` + `.dot` combination used in Live's topbar ('N/M live'); the dot is Live Red when every tile is live, Warn Amber ('wait') otherwise. Full-round, borderless (redesign v2 — border removed).
components.css: .ds-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; height: 24px; padding: 0 9px; border-radius: var(--r-full, 999px); background: var(--panel-2, #222226); font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted, #a1a1a6); white-space: nowrap; } .ds-dot { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--faint, #6e6e73); flex: none; } .ds-dot-live { background: var(--live, #ff453a); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--live-soft, rgba(255,69,58,.16)); }

components.name: Toggle Switch
components.description: The only binary on/off control style in the system — unchanged shape across the foundation pass (already fully round).
components.css: .ds-switch { position: relative; display: inline-block; width: 38px; height: 22px; } .ds-switch input { position: absolute; inset: 0; opacity: 0; margin: 0; cursor: pointer; z-index: 1; } .ds-switch span { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: var(--r-full, 999px); background: var(--line-2, #2c2c31); transition: background .15s; } .ds-switch span::after { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 3px; left: 3px; width: 16px; height: 16px; border-radius: 50%; background: #fff; transition: transform .15s; } .ds-switch input:checked + span { background: var(--accent, #0074e8); } .ds-switch input:checked + span::after { transform: translateX(16px); } .ds-switch input:focus-visible + span { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #0074e8); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Nav Link
components.description: Topbar/side-rail navigation item (icon + label). The active state uses Accent Blue Soft background with Accent Blue Text (the foreground-optimized variant) as the label color, not the fill-optimized Accent Blue itself.
components.html: Live
components.css: .ds-nav-link { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; padding: 7px 12px; border-radius: var(--r-sm, 10px); color: var(--muted, #a1a1a6); text-decoration: none; font-weight: 500; } .ds-nav-link:hover { background: var(--panel-2, #222226); color: var(--text, #f5f5f7); } .ds-nav-link-active { background: var(--accent-soft, rgba(0, 116, 232, .16)); color: var(--accent-text, #2e97ff); } .ds-nav-icon { width: 18px; height: 18px; flex: none; }

components.name: Card
components.description: The primary content container across Settings and Events — flat at rest, no shadow, a hairline border is the only separation. Corner radius widened in the foundation pass (22px, was 12px).
components.html:
Recorder connection

Address, login, and encryption.
components.css: .ds-card { background: var(--panel, #18181b); border: 1px solid var(--line, rgba(255,255,255,.09)); border-radius: var(--r-lg, 22px); padding: 18px 20px; } .ds-card h3 { margin: 0 0 3px; font-size: 14.5px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--text, #f5f5f7); } .ds-card-sub { margin: 0; color: var(--muted, #a1a1a6); font-size: 13px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard text/password/number field used across Settings.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; height: 36px; padding: 0 11px; border-radius: var(--r-sm, 10px); border: 1px solid var(--line-2, #2c2c31); background: var(--bg, #09090b); color: var(--text, #f5f5f7); font: 400 14px/1 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-input:hover { border-color: var(--faint, #6e6e73); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #0074e8); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Success Badge
components.description: The real Armed Green usage: an 'On'/'2FA' status badge (`.badge.ok`) — success/healthy state, never a live indicator. The label color is Armed Green Text, the light-theme-safe foreground variant, not the fill-optimized Armed Green.
components.css: .ds-badge-ok { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; height: 20px; padding: 0 7px; border-radius: var(--r-full, 999px); font-size: 11.5px; font-weight: 600; background: var(--armed-soft, rgba(48,209,88,.14)); border: 1px solid var(--armed, #34d399); color: var(--armed-text, #34d399); white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Glass Dialog
components.description: The glass material system (redesign v2 foundation, new): a translucent, blurred surface for chrome that floats above or sits apart from content. This exact fill/blur/border/shadow combination is shared verbatim by `.dialog`, `.menu`, `.toast`, `.savebar > div`, `.evp-dialog`, and `.auth-card`. Never applied to chrome that floats directly over continuously-live video, which keeps an opaque gradient-scrim treatment instead.
components.css: .ds-dialog { width: min(440px, 100%); padding: 20px; border-radius: var(--r-xl, 30px); background: var(--glass-fill-heavy, rgba(18,18,20,.86)); backdrop-filter: blur(40px) saturate(1.7); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(40px) saturate(1.7); border: 1px solid var(--glass-border, rgba(255,255,255,.1)); box-shadow: var(--shadow-3, 0 24px 64px -8px rgba(0,0,0,.55)), inset 0 1px 0 var(--glass-highlight, rgba(255,255,255,.06)); } .ds-dialog h3 { margin: 0 0 6px; color: var(--text, #f5f5f7); } .ds-dialog p { margin: 0; color: var(--muted, #a1a1a6); }

components.name: The Eye Mark
components.description: Signature mark (`.brand-mark`): a white ring-and-pupil iris with Live Red's record dot at the upper right, on a dark rounded tile (`#141417`, radius 30/108). The bar mark, favicon, app icons, sign-in/pairing mark and Verify header all use this one drawing; the red dot is the only identity use of Live Red.
components.css: .ds-eyemark { position: relative; display: inline-grid; place-items: center; width: 26px; height: 26px; border-radius: 7px; background: #141417; } .ds-eyemark::before { content: ''; width: 12px; height: 12px; border-radius: 50%; border: 1.5px solid #f5f5f7; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2.5px #141417, inset 0 0 0 6px #f5f5f7; } .ds-eyemark::after { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 4px; right: 4px; width: 4px; height: 4px; border-radius: 50%; background: #ff3b30; }

narrative.overview:
Redesign v2 (see `ROADMAP.md`) rebuilt the Watch Room twice. The first pass kept the pre-redesign app's dense, flat, blue-tinted architecture and only swapped its single accent color for four single-job colors. The second, larger pass — this one — rebuilt the foundation itself to actually match the approved mockups: a neutral graphite ground (not blue-tinted), glass material on floating and page chrome (not flat panel fills), a bigger and rounder radius scale topped out by fully-pill buttons (not an 8px-radius rectangle), and real press feedback. The calm, low-contrast, stare-at-it-for-hours character survives intact — spacing stays tight, numbers stay tabular, the interface still gets out of the way of the footage it exists to show — but the material language is now genuinely Apple-adjacent rather than merely re-colored.

Four colors, four jobs: a system blue for everything interactive (selected, primary, focus, in progress), red for "this is live right now," green for "this succeeded / is healthy," and purple for tamper events specifically. Status and selection never compete for the same pixel the way a single accent used to force them to.
keyCharacteristics: Dark by default (`color-scheme: dark`), with a fully-specified light theme as a first-class alternate, not an afterthought.
Four semantic colors, each with exactly one job: blue = interactive, red = live, green = success/healthy, purple = tamper. Never mixed, never decorative.

Glass material on chrome that floats above or sits apart from content (topbar, subbar, popovers, dialogs, toasts, the auth card); flat borders everywhere else. Never blurred directly over continuously-live video.
A six-step radius scale running from a 6px chip to a fully-round 999px pill — buttons, segmented controls and status pills are pills now, not rounded rectangles.
Small, functional type scale — no hero/display type anywhere; this is an instrument panel, not a marketing page.
Tabular numerals on every timestamp, clock, duration, zoom percentage, and count.

rules.name: The On-Video Invariance Rule
rules.body: Anything painted directly over live footage (badges, overlays, ROI boxes, floating transport controls) stays fixed across light/dark theme and never gets glass/blur — the video itself never re-themes and is itself the "material" there.

rules.name: The One-Job-Per-Color Rule
rules.body: Accent Blue is the only color used for emphasis, selection, or primary action — if a control isn't active, selected, or the primary action in its group, it does not get colored, it stays graphite/muted. Live Red, Armed Green and Tamper Purple are each scoped the same way to their own single status meaning; none of the four ever stands in for another. A mode-switch button whose own label already states which mode you're in (e.g. the live view's Overview/Grid toggle) is *not* a "selected option" and does not get the pressed-accent treatment, even though it sets `aria-pressed` for assistive tech — that treatment means "this is the choice among several," not "this button is currently on."

rules.name: The Fill-vs-Text Rule
rules.body: A semantic color has two numerically distinct values when it's used both as a filled background (optimized for white/ink text on top of it) and as foreground text elsewhere (Accent Blue vs. Accent Blue Text, Armed Green vs. Armed Green Text in light theme) — never assume a fill color passes as text just because the fill itself is accessible.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every numeric read-out — the clock, timestamps, durations, zoom percentage, event counts — uses `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, so digits never shift width as they change on a screen meant to be glanced at repeatedly.

rules.name: The Floating-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: If it's part of the normal page layout at rest, it's flat with a hairline border. A layer floats above or apart from the page → Float or Shadow-3, usually with Glass. A live-grid tile or Events card has the pointer directly on it → Hover-Lift, and only while the pointer stays there. Nothing else gets a shadow.

rules.name: The Glass-Over-One-Stream Rule
rules.body: Glass may sit over video only where there is one stream on screen (Focus, full-screen Playback) and only while that chrome is visible — it fades on idle, so continuous backdrop-filter recomputation over moving footage is limited to the moments someone is using the controls. Never across the multi-tile grid.

rules.name: The Pill-for-Status-and-Action Rule
rules.body: Full-round shape is reserved for things you act on or that represent a state — buttons, segmented controls, status pills, event badges, quality tags, toggles. Containers that hold content — cards, tiles, dialogs — never go fully round; they stay in the 16–30px range.

dos: Do treat each of the four semantic colors as a state signal first — reach for Accent Blue when something is selected, primary, or on; Live Red only for live status; Armed Green only for success/healthy; never as general brand color to sprinkle around.
Do use Accent Blue Text / Armed Green Text (not the fill color) whenever a semantic color is the *foreground* of text or an icon rather than a filled background.
Do keep numeric displays (clocks, timestamps, durations, percentages, counts) on tabular numerals.
Do keep containers flat with a hairline border; reserve glass + Float/Shadow-3 strictly for chrome that floats above or sits apart from the page.
Do use full-round shape for buttons, segmented controls, status/selection chips, and toggles — never for content containers (cards, tiles, dialogs stay in the 16–30px range).
donts: Don't introduce a fifth semantic hue for "brand" purposes — warn-amber, danger-red and info-teal stay semantic-only.
Don't add shadow to any surface that's part of the normal page flow at rest (cards, tiles, panels) — that's reserved for floating/glass layers and the hover-lift exception.
Don't put glass/`backdrop-filter` over the multi-tile grid, or keep it over a single stream once its chrome has faded (see the Glass-Over-One-Stream Rule).
Don't add a display/hero type size anywhere; this is an Operate-mode instrument panel, not a marketing surface, and the type scale stays functional.

Don't give a mode-switch button (one whose own label already states which mode is active, like Overview/Grid) the pressed-accent treatment — that treatment means "the selected option among several," not "this is currently on."
